units.text: E C 2 automatic recovery addresses supported underlying host failures that cause a system status check to fail. An instance status check failure by itself does not trigger this recovery. First identify which check failed.

The recovery illustration preserves the instance I D, assigned addresses, placement group, attached E B S volumes and Availability Zone. But the operating system restarts and memory is lost. A CloudWatch recovery action also loses instance-store data. Verify eligibility for the chosen recovery method.

A stop and start can change an automatically assigned public IPv4 address; an Auto Scaling replacement is a different instance. Neither is the recovery shown here. Verify recovery support in advance, monitor outcomes, and keep backups and application recovery procedures.

Choose storage by how the workload reads and writes. Instance store is fast, local scratch, so checkpoint valuable work elsewhere. E B S provides persistent block storage; check volume and instance limits. S3 holds durable datasets and results as objects, not a native POSIX filesystem.

E F S provides shared N F S access for many clients. Its throughput mode is not provisioned I O operations per second. F S x for Lustre is suited to highly parallel file access and can integrate with S3 to stage data and export results.

Match compute, filesystem throughput, metadata access and durability to the same job. Test the actual layout, including data staging and checkpoints, rather than relying on a headline throughput figure.

AWS Batch starts with jobs and their resource requirements. Queues and scheduling dispatch them into eligible compute environments. For multi-node parallel jobs, coordinate multiple E C 2 nodes using supported compute; Spot and Fargate aren't supported for that job type.

ParallelCluster provisions and manages a configured H P C cluster, including compute, network, scheduler and shared storage. Choose it when the team needs a cluster and supported scheduler workflow like Slurm rather than only managed job execution.

Independent rendering tasks can retry separately. A multi-node M P I simulation needs coordinated nodes and suitable communication. A scheduler, a cluster configuration tool, and an application communication library solve different problems.

Trace the unhealthy instance from left to right. HealthCheck marks it unhealthy. ReplaceUnhealthy calls Terminate and then Launch. If a load balancer is attached, AddToLoadBalancer registers the replacement.
The right panel lists other independent processes: alarm-driven actions, zone rebalancing, instance refresh, and scheduled actions. They do not all do the same job as health marking or replacement.
Start with the process that corresponds to what failed. Missing registration is different from a failed launch. Suspending one process does not pause the fleet or every other process.

With Launch suspended, scale-out can't add instances; replacement may still terminate unhealthy instances without launching successors. With ReplaceUnhealthy suspended instead, health checks can still mark an instance unhealthy, but replacement waits until that process resumes.

If AddToLoadBalancer was suspended, missed registrations aren't automatically added on resume. Register those instances explicitly when appropriate. A scheduled action missed during suspension doesn't replay.

Check capacity, health, registration and pending work before restoring controls. Resuming can trigger replacement or rebalancing. Suspending Terminate does not prevent EC2 Spot from interrupting a Spot instance.
Rolling instance refresh replaces instances in the same Auto Scaling group using an updated launch template version. Set healthy-capacity and warmup controls, and verify what rollback is supported.

For separate old and new fleets, use weighted target groups on an Application Load Balancer, or separate load balancers and weighted DNS records. Check the new fleet before increasing its share. DNS caches make DNS rollback non-instantaneous.

Keep isolated test access and enough old fleet capacity for recovery. Check sessions and schema compatibility. Sending traffic back does not undo a database migration or restore lost application state.

The Spot Fleet request can include Spot and optional On-Demand capacity. Pools vary by instance type, operating system and Availability Zone, and instance weights express useful capacity units. A target is a request, not a promise.

Price capacity optimized weighs capacity availability and price. Capacity optimized prioritizes stronger available pools; diversified spreads across specified pools. Lowest price emphasizes cheaper capacity and can increase interruption risk. None of these removes interruption risk.

Distinguish legacy Spot Fleet from an Auto Scaling mixed-instances policy. For ongoing lifecycle management, consider Auto Scaling. If you need to manage instance lifecycle yourself, AWS recommends E C 2 Fleet over legacy Spot Fleet.

Route Fifty-Three resolves the shop's hostname; it is not in the HTTP data path. The browser connects to CloudFront. For the image path, a cache hit is served at the edge, while a miss fetches from the S3 origin.

Order posts aren't cached. Their CloudFront behavior forwards to an Application Load Balancer, then to the Auto Scaling app. The app writes to DynamoDB and sends an order event to S Q S. A separate worker polls for and processes it asynchronously.

Choose an Application Load Balancer for HTTP host or path decisions, or a Network Load Balancer for a suitable Layer Four workload. Use Lambda for bounded event work and E C 2 or containers for persistent applications. Pick for the job, not just the service name.

Start with the orders request in the top row. If the requirement is to inspect an H T T P host, path, or header, choose an Application Load Balancer. It can forward to a Lambda target in this example without requiring a Lambda function URL.

The game session in the middle needs T C P transport rather than path matching. Choose a Network Load Balancer for that type of flow. If a stable address is required, check its static I P support and the Elastic I P option for an internet-facing balancer.

The bottom path inserts a firewall or inspection appliance into the I P route. That is Gateway Load Balancer. It uses Geneve encapsulation to deliver traffic to appliances. Choose from traffic and routing first, then verify target type and health checks.

Follow the client's orders request. The Application Load Balancer listener accepts H T T P S on port four forty-three and uses a T L S certificate. The listener answers the first question: on what protocol and port do we accept traffic?
The rule checks the request path. Slash orders followed by the order ID matches this example, so the rule forwards to the Orders target group. A different path can match a different rule.

The group contains registered I P targets and checks slash health. It sends this request to the healthy address shown. The response returns to the client through the load balancer; the bottom arrow summarizes that return, not a direct client connection to the target.

Here the internet client reaches only the internet-facing load balancer on H T T P S port four forty-three. The load balancer uses public subnets in both Availability Zones. Check public routing and the load balancer security group for that listener.

The application instances stay in private subnets. The load balancer connects to them on the configured application and health-check ports. In this example their security group allows those connections from the load balancer security group, not from internet clients.

The dashed red path is not an allowed direct connection. Verify both the client-to-load-balancer path and load-balancer-to-target path, including target registration and health. Making the load balancer public does not make its targets public.
On the left, cross-zone balancing is off. A load balancer node only chooses targets in its own Availability Zone. The node in zone A cannot use the healthy zone B targets for that flow.

On the right, a node can pick healthy targets in the other enabled zone as well. This changes the target pool. It does not mean the client connects straight to a target or that one load balancer node hands the connection to another.

The Application Load Balancer has cross-zone on at the load-balancer level; a supported target group can turn it off. A Network Load Balancer defaults to off and can enable it. Keep enough healthy capacity in each zone rather than using the feature as a substitute.

Follow the periodic probe to slash health on the application port. With a matcher expecting two hundred, target A passes. Target B times out, and target C returns five oh three. Targets normally need to pass the configured checks to receive new requests.

The target-health details distinguish timeout from response-code mismatch. For a timeout, check the connection path and whether the app responds in time. For an unexpected response code, check the readiness handler and its dependencies. An open port alone does not prove readiness.

Read the warning: if the group has only unhealthy registered targets across its enabled zones, the Application Load Balancer can fail open and send requests to those unhealthy targets. Monitor the health signal and plan recovery; do not rely on health checks alone to protect the application.

The listener accepts the request, then evaluates its rules from lowest priority number first. The order example matches both the A P I host and the orders path, and forwards to the Orders target group.

The shop host and images path match a different rule. The Images target group contains application targets that use S three behind them; the bucket itself is not a direct Application Load Balancer target.

No rule matches the third request, so the default action returns the fixed four oh four shown. Host and path are the only conditions used in this example. Routing picks the destination; it does not replace authentication or target authorization.
